key_insight: Robot policies may need access to visual processing as it unfolds—not just a final compressed image representation. NEO-VLA is introduced toward this goal, aiming to preserve details that matter for manipulation.
problem_solved: Visual encoders can compress away local geometry, object boundaries, depth cues, and subtle state changes before action reasoning begins, potentially limiting precise robotic manipulation.
method: Reexamines the standard pipeline in which visual encoding finishes before action reasoning starts.
Introduces NEO-VLA toward policies that directly access evolving visual computation; the truncated abstract does not provide architectural or evaluation details.
impact: This direction could help practitioners design robot policies that retain task-critical visual information. Performance gains and implementation requirements cannot be assessed from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: compressed visual endpoint versus action reasoning connected to evolving visual processing.
Annotated manipulation scene highlighting edges, geometry, depth cues, and subtle state changes.
Information bottleneck illustration showing important visual details lost during compression.
Conceptual feedback diagram linking visual processing stages with action decisions.
paper_title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
paper_authors: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu, Siyuan Hu, Ziqi Huang
